newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may see tiny carryover coffee stock - Unicafe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may see tiny carryover coffee stock - Unicafe.

text.p: Brazilian carryover coffee stocks in private hands could be as low as 39,000 60-kg bags at the end of the 1996/97 crop year (July/June), said leading coffee exporter Unicafe.

This would represent a sharp fall from the 876,000 bags Unicafe estimates was carried over from 1995/96 and would be dramatically lower than the 8.35 million bags calculated to have been in private hands as of June 30, 1995.
The stock calculation is using Unicafe's second estimate of the 1996/97 coffee crop of 26 million bags and considering a 1995/96 harvest of 14.6 million bags.
Based on forecasts by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) however, carryover stocks could be 2.74 million bags by the end of June this year.
This is due to higher crop forecasts of 16.8 million bags in 1995/96 and 27.5 million bags in 1996/97.
The minimal stock carryover estimated by Unicafe is working on the basis of a total of 850,000 bags sold in government auctions in the first half of 1997.
"This is what we think will be the minimum sold by the government," said Unicafe's president Jair Coser.
The private sector is hoping the government will at least increase monthly auctions of government stocks to the current limit of 200,000 bags, and ideally to raise sales to above this.

Unicafe estimates exports in the first half of next year to total seven million bags - in theory six million bags of green coffee beans as agreed with other producing countries and one million bags of soluble coffee.

"In reality however, I don't think that green coffee exports will reach six million bags. Rather I think that green exports will be around 5.6 million or 5.7 million bags and that soluble coffee shipments will make up the rest," Coser said.
